answer: Each agent commits 64 GB of RAM and proves live ownership with memory-bus latency probes: the verifier sends pseudo-random addresses and demands sub-120 ns replies, so one honest agent holding its own harbor array passes while ten clones sharing a single DIMM queue and miss every deadline. Ten separate 64 GB rigs cost about $9,000 against $900 for one honest node. The chain seals probe transcripts into the epoch record, and three failed probes slash the bond and freeze the pearl seat for an epoch while terrace auditors replay timings to rule out cached replies.
